To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ATF3 and the combination of ATF 3, STAT3, Smad 1 and c-Jun promote regeneration in the central branch of sensory axons but without synergistic effect, and that these TFs do promote functional regeneration after dorsal root injury.
overexpression of ATF3 alone, but not the combination of ATF, c-Jun, Smad1 and STAT3, promoted regeneration of the central branch of sensory neurons after dorsal root transections.
overexpression of ATF3 alone, but not the combination of ATF, c-Jun, Smad1 and STAT3, is able to promote faster regeneration of central axon branch in the absence of peripheral nerve lesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regeneration of sensory nerves after injury, which is a significant problem for patients with spinal cord injuries.
the molecular mechanisms of regeneration of the central branch of sensory neurons and how this may be manipulated to improve regeneration in vivo.
the regeneration of sensory nerves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of ATF-3, Smad-1, c-Jun and STAT3 does not induce a regeneration programme in the absence of peripheral nerve lesion.

ATF3 and the combination of ATF, c-Jun, Smad1 and STAT3 are able to promote regeneration of the injured axon, but do not induce the regeneration programme in the absence of peripheral nerve injury and do not lead to functional recovery after dorsal root injury.
ATF3 is sufficient to promote axon regeneration in DRG neurons but that the combination of these TFs is not more effective than ATF3 alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the overexpression of ATF3, STAT3, Smad and c-Jun is sufficient to promote regeneration of the proximal part of the axon, but not the distal part, and that the overexpression does not induce functional recovery.
overexpression of ATF3 alone or the combination of TF's can promote regeneration of the proximal central axon branch but not regeneration of the distal axon branch.
ATF3 alone and in combination with other factors, is sufficient for promoting the regeneration of the central branch of sensory neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
while TFs are key regulators of the RAG programme, the combination of TF expression is not necessarily additive or synergistic.
the combination of ATF-3, Smad-1, STAT-3 and c-Jun can promote regeneration after dorsal root injury but not in the presence of a complete lesion.

overexpression of these RAG TFs is sufficient to induce a regeneration-like response in DRG neurons in vitro but not in vivo, and that the combination of TF expression does not lead to synergistic effects on regeneration.
